newsitem.title: USA: Panenergy says plans new NYC natgas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Panenergy says plans new NYC natgas pipeline.

text.p: PanEnergy Corp said Thursday it plans to develop a natural gas pipeline that will increase delivery capability into New York City by almost 25 percent.

The ExcelsiorSM pipeline project will provide 500,000 Dekatherms per day of natural gas deliveries from a new Texas Eastern Transmission Corp pipeline connection in New Jersey, across lower New York Bay to Long Island near John F. Kennedy International Airport, said the company.

The project will create a new natural gas delivery system into Long Island for further distribution by Brooklyn Union Gas Co, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc and Long Island Lighting Co, which comprise the New York Facilities Group.
The Excelsior project will consist of 44 miles of 30-inch diameter pipeline, most of which will be offshore. The Excelsior pipeline is expected to be in service by November 2000.
